claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is controlled by a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition in the operative plasticity mechanism.
At higher temperatures and lower strain rates, plasticity in FeNiCrMn is primarily accommodated by dislocation glide.
Lower temperature and/or higher strain rate progressively activates deformation twinning in FeNiCrMn.
The low-temperature/high-strain-rate regime produces a higher twin-boundary density relative to dislocation structures.
Deformation twins provide additional barriers to dislocation motion.
Twin-induced barriers increase strain hardening in FeNiCrMn.
The glide-to-twinning transition reinforces the strength-ductility balance.
Yield strength increases under low-temperature and high-strain-rate conditions.
The increase in yield strength is accompanied by a higher density of deformation twins.
FeNiCrMn exhibits increased strain-rate sensitivity associated with a shift in its dominant deformation mechanism.
Using identically prepared specimens with the same initial microstructure can isolate the effects of testing temperature and strain rate.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from approximately 77 K to 1073 K and from about 10^-3 s^-1 to at least 10^3 s^-1.
Adiabatic shear banding may dominate outside the proposed strain-rate regime.
Oxidation may dominate outside the proposed high-temperature boundary.
The precise temperature or strain rate at which twinning becomes dominant is not defined.
Residual impurities or slight microstructural variations may influence the response.

contradictions.description: The conditions and baseline say that only temperature and strain rate are varied, but the design also varies loading mode between tension and compression and uses different test configurations, so temperature and strain rate are not literally the only experimental variables.
